Katya Cuevas, Alliyah Douglass 
 Delegation From Allied Gardens, San Diego 
 The Republic of Latvia 
 Commission on the Status of Women 
 Violence Against Indigenous Women in the Amazon 
 Section I 
 Women all over the world face violence but one place affected by this sexual violence is 
 the Amazon. As representatives of Latvia, we do not support sexual violence against women as it 
 is a criminal offense in Latvia. Something that we do to help women and girls who have been 
 raped or sexually abused is we have social rehabilitation services. These rehabilitation homes 
 have been financed by the state and have been proven to help victims.  1  Just like in Latvia, sexual 
 abuse is illegal in most amazonian places. The women are not just fighting for the forests but 
 also their rights as human beings. More people need to be informed about what is going on if we 
 want to solve these problems. I say this because when people hear more about the issues these 
 women are having, they feel empathy and try to help them. For example, when a journalist heard 
 about what was going on in the amazon, she immediately tried to help. 
 Now, she is part of an alliance of women who opened a safe home for women and girls 
 who have fled sexual violence and violence facing activists fighting for the amazon rainforests. 
 This specific safe house lies in Ecuador and it is it’s first of its kind to treat violence against 
 women, especially indigenous women. The founder of this safe house created it because she 
 realized that minors and deforestation groups were causing harm not just to the environment but 
 to the people who live in the rainforest, especially the women and girls. In other words, she 
 realized that the minors weren’t only affecting the economy, but they were abusing the women 
 and girls in the amazon because the people needed more money and food, and the minors 
 could provide that. One important thing to note is that by asking yourself questions you can 
 figure out how to help others. For example, these women

 asked themselves, “How can we support indigenous women,” and “How can we collectively 
 heal?” By asking these questions, we can figure out ways to solve these problems.  2 
 Rehabilitation homes have not only given women new and safer houses, but they have 
 also provided legal support. Additionally, this is even more effective because it is a community 
 of women who have all gone through the same problems. One way that these homes help abused 
 women is by creating a support system where the women listened to what everyone had to say. 
 As the amount of domestic violence rises, the need for houses like these, especially in the 
 Amazon, rises. With violence rising, there are more and more attacks that lead to trauma for 
 indigenous people. 
 Because some of the women are activists trying to stop minors and other people from 
 destroying their homelands, they face more risks. One website compares information between six 
 different indigenous women living in the Amazon and shows what types and reasons for their 
 abuse/violence. The graph showed that 5 out of 6 of the women’s violence was caused by 
 Personal Relationship as Resistance’s space (PR) and Female Leadership (FL). These two 
 occurred the most often but there were thirty-six other reasons and some happened more than 
 once.  3 
 Victims say that it is hard to achieve justice for multiple reasons. Some of these are 
 because of corruption or sexism but one of the most common reasons is simply because they live

 too far away from proper authorities that will do something when they report sexual violence. 
 Sometimes, threats come from these women’s communities. There is violence on all fronts of the 
 world that women live in and we need to do something to decrease the amount of sexual 
 violence. Six in ten women who have reported being assaulted have experienced some form of 
 sexual violence. Additionally, of the other four women in that ten, at least two of them have 
 experienced sexual violence, they just do not want to admit it. 
 Sexual assault prevention programs have been used for a long time in almost every 
 country. These programs have mainly been focussing on what not to do but this has not shown to 
 help. Teachers have taught both victims and the attacker about the consequences of sexual assault 
 but as previously stated, these methods have not made a big difference in the amount of sexual 
 and domestic violence in this world. One program that is the opposite of the one stated above is 
 the healthy relationship approach to this problem. This approach teaches people what a healthy 
 relationship is and how to maintain one. It helps others respect their partners and provide fewer 
 reasons for sexual abuse, therefore, creating lower accounts of it. The relationships these 
 programs talk about are not just dating or married ones, they are also family and business 
 relationships because those are also different causes of violence.  4

 Section II 
 Latvia has worked extremely hard to get rid of its domestic violence and protect victims 
 of violence. Furthermore, the country is currently looking to find a way to ratify the Istanbul 
 Convention.  5  The Istanbul Convention was created to  stop combat and domestic violence. This 
 convention sets a standard that saves millions of girls' and women’s lives. In other words, this is 
 a group of people who create a treaty every 5 years that stop religion and gender-based violence. 
 This treaty specifically targets violence against women and girls. This treaty sets a minimum 
 standard for governments in Europe. These minimum standards consist of prevention, protection, 
 and prosecution of domestic and sexual violence against women and girls. The convention also 
 sets rules about protection and support services that every state has to follow. These rules consist 
 of; a reasonable number of shelters, rape crisis centers, free helplines that you can reach at any 
 hour of the day, psychological counseling, and health care for any survivors of sexual violence, 
 forcing governments to ensure education about gender  equality, healthy relationships, and 
 sexuality. This is key legislation to ensure that if violence occurs, there is a process to help 
 women who have experienced it. Finally, one of the most important things in this constitution is 
 that lesbian, bisexual, transgender women, and intersex people who face or have faced hostility 
 all over Europe are entitled to protection and all of the other things that come with this treaty too. 
 One more thing to add to that statement is that refugees and immigrants are also protected from

 this constitution if the country they live in has signed this constitution. Latvia is a part of the 
 Istanbul Convention and so are lots of other countries in Europe such as Ukraine and Germany.  6 
 One important thing to know about Latvia is we have tried and mainly achieved gender 
 equality. We have even had a woman as a president and a prime minister. On that note, Latvia 
 has experts studying gender equality and how to achieve it. Since 2014, Latvia has worked 
 extremely hard to create a legal framework to reduce the amount of domestic violence and 
 protect the victims of it. By educating the people in Latvia, we have successfully created more 
 awareness and helped people realize how wrong sexual violence is. The Criminal Procedure Law 
 has been updated and strengthened to have much more safeguards and chances for victims to 
 report abusers. Latvia also believes that a full understanding of women's rights is essential for the 
 commitment to the Beijing Platform for Action. The government has focused its resources on 
 creating gender equality, especially in areas of education, and work/labor, which is important for 
 smart, sustainable, and inclusive growth.  7 
 The Beijing Platform for Action declaration is an agenda for the empowerment of 
 women. It is also one of the basis to analyze the situation women are in around the world and 
 know what places are doing to support women’s empowerment. The Beijing Platform for Action 
 started in 1995 and includes over 40,000 government delegates, representatives, and experts 
 from all over the world. This action creates the commitment of the international community and

 They are trying to achieve gender equality and provide better experiences and opportunities for 
 both women and girls. 
 The platform of action helps women and girls globally who have or currently are fighting 
 for gender equality and women's rights. This law is still important today because we have not 
 fully achieved gender equality and that is something that we are working towards. It also sets an 
 agenda for governments, organizations, and the private sector to safeguard women’s rights as 
 humans and they make sure gender is taken into account in all policies and programs. The 
 Beijing Platform for Action is reviewed by CSW every five years and they have taken reports 
 every year to show how the action has been working and what has to change or be improved.  8 
 As was previously stated, Latvia is now part of the Beijing Platform for Action and is working 
 hard to have gender equality in its states. 
 Section III 
 The Delegation of Latvia has created two different solutions for this problem. Solution 1: 
 Our first proposed solution is to create more safe houses in the Amazon for women and girls who 
 have or are currently facing sexual or domestic violence. These houses would provide a 
 community for these women to feel safe in hence the name and get a start at a better life. The 
 women and girls are allowed to bring their children or siblings with them if they are also a threat 
 to violence whether it be sexual or just domestic. These children would still get all the same

 benefits of the safe house that the women and girls get. The women and girls living in these safe 
 houses would have access to counseling, health care, a job, and better education and legal 
 support. We would provide these things by having counselors from other states/ countries come 
 in and live inside our residencies and give these women 24/7 care or counseling. We would also 
 have nurses and doctors from other countries/ states who can volunteer to leave where they 
 currently are to help these women and girls. Each person would get paid a small amount of 
 money per day but they would get access to healthcare, a place to live, and education for their 
 families. A job that a victim can have before they are ready to go back to normal life is taking 
 care of the kids in the nursery or being a teacher. We also have actual educators but in some 
 cases, women who were abused were teachers or cared for children in their native land and want 
 to keep doing that. We would accept any person needing assistance, even if they are LGBTQ+. In 
 our safe houses, we have people from newborn babies to women who are in their 40s or 50s. We 
 also take volunteers of women in the community who would like to help out and make women 
 feel more at home. Each house will be able to have about 20-30 staff members and 40-50 
 victims. These houses will be all over the Amazon and they will help victims go back to their 
 normal lives. 
 Our second proposed solution is to educate children more about sexual harassment, 
 domestic violence, and healthy relationships so we can stop it at an early age. This program 
 would be called, “Take a Stand.” Take a Stand would go to schools and communities in the 
 amazon to start and then maybe in the future around the world to explain to kids what sexual 
 violence is and why it is a bad thing. It would also explain how to stay in a healthy relationship

 and what that is. This program is fundamental to make sure that future generations do not have 
 sexual violence and to create gender equality for all. Take a stand would focus on the most 
 important problems under the umbrella of sexual violence and explain to kids ages 10-18 why 
 this happens, how it is wrong, and what they can do to stop it. The whole program will be kid 
 friendly and will not discuss any topics that are too harsh or violent for the kid's age group. It 
 will also be understandable so that no kids are left questioning anything about this program and 
 if they are then, we can answer their questions. We can also give them ways if they would like to 
 help victims like making cards with thoughtful messages in them to make the victims feel safe. 
 With the older side of the group, we will also go over how to report being sexually harassed and 
 that no matter what the abuser says, it is still good to report. We will also provide them with legal 
 help if any of them were ever abused or hurt. The teachers of these lessons would understand 
 every native language and be teachers/ friendly people so the students are not startled. The 
 teachers will get paid a lot of money coming from the world bank and their hotel and plane 
 tickets will also be paid for. They will also get the experience of going to these native places in 
 the Amazon and seeing how these people live in rustic areas different from our own.

 Delegation From Allied Gardens, San Diego 
 The Republic of Latvia 
 Commission on the Status of Women 
 Legal Clothing Restrictions on Women 
 Section I 
 Clothing regulations that prevent women from dressing how they prefer to instill sexist 
 stereotypes that must be addressed. Dress codes and clothing regulations have been implemented 
 and inferred by society and the government for hundreds of years. However, now that we are in 
 modern times, these regulations are outdated, clearly sexist, and often xenophobic. To specify, a 
 study in America shows that 86 percent of professionals and 80 percent of managers scrutinize 
 that clothing choices affect the chance of promotion. Also, a study on a large North American 
 retail chain shows that women in the workforce are 14 percent less likely to be promoted to a 
 better position. This is definitive evidence showing the influence a woman's clothing has on her 
 position at work, no matter the progress she has made. This clearly conveys that it is a crucial 
 problem to address because it strips women of their right to freedom of expression and creates 
 more conflicts than it solves. For instance, in Iran, the punishment for not wearing the hijab 
 correctly is up to two months in prison with a fine. Recently, Masha Amini was killed in Iranian 
 police custody for not wearing her hijab correctly, so protests have erupted causing over 400 
 protesters to be killed and about 18,000 arrests. There are also countries that require women to 
 wear less clothing. For example, France has banned all burqas and niqabs. In 2004 they also 
 excluded all headscarves, hijabs, and religious symbols from state schools and government 
 buildings. This caused conflict with the Muslim community in France; the UN Human Rights 
 Committee states that a ban on face veils is inconsistent with International Law and Human 
 Rights definitive standards, considering it discriminatory. In addition,  the International Covenant 
 on Civil and Political Rights has stated that averting women from wearing a head scarf or hijab 
 in France is against their customs and standards. In brief, the opinion of ICCP and ILHR show 
 that dress codes that are inferred or coded in law are not up to modern standards for women's 
 rights. 
 Katya Cuevas, Alliyah Douglass 
 Delegation From Allied Gardens, San Diego 
 The Republic of Latvia 
 Commission on the Status of Women 
 Legal Clothing Restrictions on Women 
 Section II 
 Like many other European countries, Latvia has recognized the importance of women's 
 rights and safety. Latvia has taken many extensive measures to ensure women's rights to get an 
 exemplary score on the GII (Gender Inequality Index). For instance, the Constitution of the 
 Republic of Latvia states, "all humans in Latvia are equal before the law and the courts. Human 
 rights are being exercised without any discrimination whatsoever.” Latvia does not have many 
 clear policies that ensure their opinion on dress codes and regulations, but we can infer from the 
 policies and information that we do have that Latvia has a strong belief in women having the 
 right to their own clothing choices as long as it is not a safety precaution physically or culturally. 
 For example, in 2016, Latvia implemented a legal ban on burquas and Islamic face veil 
 coverings, even though only three women within the country were known to wear them. It was 
 clarified later on that this ban was not put in place for public safety but instead to preserve 
 Latvian cultural values and to give public space to individuals. This policy isn’t uncommon in 
 other European countries allied with Latvia; such as France, Denmark, and Belgium. For 
 exemplification, France and Latvia are both participating members of the European Union and 
 NATO. They have both implemented the ban on the burqa for various reasons such as public 
 safety and the protection of European merit. Latvia has no other clear laws or policies that relate 
 to dress codes, but they do have social expectations for what the general public should wear. 
 Multiple sources state that business attire for Latvian women includes jackets with trousers pants 
 or skirts. This should be unproblematic of business expectations, but in Lavia what a woman 
 wears does state status. This causes many Latvian women to be pressured to wear gold jewelry, 
 expensive clothing, shoes, and accessories. It is also said that many Latvian women wear strong 
 perfumes to work to make good impressions. These are very common work standards although 
 they could be improved. 
 Katya Cuevas, Alliyah Douglass

 Section III 
 Latvia has been involved in helping solve women's rights for many years by increasing women's 
 wages in underrepresented work areas and implementing the  Concept Paper on Gender Equality 
 Implementation (2001). But, there are many ways Latvia can expand its support towards 
 women's rights. For example, Latvia can help secure funds to create refugee centers for women 
 and children in countries that have enforced dress codes and laws that prevent women from 
 living in safe environments. For instance, in Iranian women are forced to cover most of their 
 bodies and wear the hijab. There are serious consequences for women who do not wear the hijab 
 correctly, and women have died trying to protest these unjust dress codes. To further articulate 
 my resolution, according to UNHCR’s data, the most common destinations for Iranian refugees 
 are Canada, Germany, and the United Kingdom, all of which are allies of Latvia. Giving funds to 
 help improve and create new and more available refugee centers in these places would make it 
 easier for the refugees to start their new life. Giving funds to this cause would help support 
 families to get jobs, healthcare, and housing. This would also help the lack of employment that 
 refugees and immigrants face. This would also pose an attainable solution for countries like 
 Sudan, Saudi Arabia, Lybia, and Iraq, which also have strict and enforced dress codes for 
 women. This possible resolution helps women in countries where religious attire is enforced, but 
 it doesn’t completely resolve the problem of dress codes. It excludes places where attire that 
 shows religious symbols is seen as a negative clothing choice. For example, Orthodox Jewish 
 women often get seen by the public as too restrictive and can get shamed for their traditional way 
 of life. This is also common with other religious groups that infer more modest clothing such as 
 Morman, Amish, Orthodox Christian, and Muslim communities. A way that Latvia could involve 
 itself to prevent this from happening within its own country would be to publicly advertise a 
 plethora of minority religions that don’t get positively recognized by the public. This would 
 expose Latvian citizens to more diverse religions and ideologies, strengthening Latvia as a 
 whole. We could get funding for advertisements and events by creating public functions, 
 fundraisers, and fun activities that will educate and involve the public. In total, these resolutions 
 positively affect Latvia and its allies, nourishing their relations to a further extent while helping 
 women from across the world reach a new point of religious and expressive freedom.
